data.title: Topical corticosteroids — overview & potency
data.summary: IV Topical corticosteroids · Glucocorticoids for skin use; classified by potency (vasoconstrictor assay)
data.body:
_Topicals · IV Topical corticosteroids_

**Class:** Glucocorticoids for skin use; classified by potency (vasoconstrictor assay)

## Mechanism of action
- Anti-inflammatory: switch off NF-κB/AP-1-driven cytokines; induce lipocortin → less arachidonic acid → fewer prostaglandins and leukotrienes
- Immunosuppressive: reduce Langerhans cells, T-cell activation
- Antiproliferative (epidermis and fibroblasts) — useful in psoriasis, harmful as atrophy
- Vasoconstrictive — basis of the McKenzie–Stoughton potency assay

## Pharmacokinetics
- Absorption increases with: higher potency, ointment base, occlusion, thin skin (face, eyelids, genitals, flexures — up to 30–40 times forearm), inflamed skin, infants and elderly, large area
- Halogenation (fluorination) increases potency and side effects

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- US 7-class system (most to least potent):
- Class 1 (super-potent): clobetasol propionate 0.05%, halobetasol propionate 0.05%, augmented betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% ointment
- Class 2 (high): mometasone furoate 0.1% ointment, fluocinonide 0.05%, desoximetasone 0.25%
- Class 3 (high): betamethasone valerate 0.1% ointment, fluticasone propionate 0.005% ointment
- Class 4 (medium): mometasone furoate 0.1% cream, triamcinolone acetonide 0.1% ointment, fluocinolone 0.025% ointment
- Class 5 (medium–low): triamcinolone 0.1% cream/lotion, fluticasone 0.05% cream, betamethasone valerate 0.1% cream, hydrocortisone valerate/butyrate
- Class 6 (low): desonide 0.05%, fluocinolone 0.01%, alclometasone 0.05%
- Class 7 (least potent): hydrocortisone 1–2.5% (acetate or base)
- UK/India often use a 4-class system: very potent (clobetasol), potent (betamethasone valerate, mometasone), moderate (clobetasone butyrate), mild (hydrocortisone)

## Dose & formulations
- Fingertip unit (FTU): ribbon from the tip of an adult index finger to the first crease ≈ 0.5 g, covers about 2 adult palms (2% BSA)
- Once or twice daily; once daily is usually enough for potent steroids (reservoir effect)
- Super-potent: no more than 50 g/week and usually 2 weeks continuous use, then taper or switch to pulsed weekend therapy
- Face, flexures, genitals, children: low/medium potency, short courses
- Weekend (proactive) therapy twice weekly prevents eczema flares
- Tachyphylaxis — loss of effect with continuous use; use intermittent schedules

## Adverse effects
- Local: atrophy, striae (irreversible), telangiectasia, purpura, hypopigmentation, hypertrichosis
- Steroid acne, rosacea-like and perioral dermatitis
- Masking of infection: tinea incognito (steroid-modified tinea — a major problem in India), scabies incognito, worsening of herpes/molluscum/demodex
- Topical steroid withdrawal/dependence ('red skin'); topical steroid-damaged face (TSDF) from misuse of creams as fairness products
- Allergic contact dermatitis to the steroid (suspect when eczema does not improve; budesonide, tixocortol are markers)
- Periocular use: glaucoma, cataract
- Systemic: HPA suppression, iatrogenic Cushing, growth retardation in children (large area, potent, occlusion, infants)

## Contraindications
- Untreated skin infections (bacterial, fungal, viral, scabies), rosacea, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris, ulcerated skin
- Potent steroids on face, flexures, genitals and in infants (except under specialist guidance)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Mild–moderate steroids are safe; potent/super-potent steroids over large areas are linked to low birth weight — use the lowest potency for the shortest time.

## Viva points
- Know 1–2 examples for each class
- FTU = 0.5 g; 1 FTU covers 2 palms
- Clobetasol: max 50 g/week, 2 weeks
- Tinea incognito and TSDF — the Indian steroid misuse problem; irrational antifungal–steroid FDCs
- Contact allergy to steroids — suspect when eczema fails to respond

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.45 (Topical corticosteroids); Khopkar ch.22 (Topical and intralesional corticosteroids). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
